subject: Detection probability varies between models with the same detection covariates

messages.author: e452970a8244a89b
messages.subject: Detection probability varies between models with the same detection covariates
parts:
Hello fellow unmarked users/fans,
  I am using DISTSAMP to estimate the abundance of birds.  I just ran two models with the same detection covariates but different abundance covariates:

Model1<-distsamp(~Time+Obs~1,keyfun="hazard", unitsOut="ha", output="density",data=umf)
 Model2<-distsamp(~Time+Obs~Year+Mgmt,keyfun="hazard", unitsOut="ha", output="density",data=umf)
  
Then for each I ran code to estimate detection probabilities:

 shape<-exp(coef(Model1,type="det"))
  scale<-exp(coef(Model1,type="scale"))
  ea<-2*pi*integrate(grhaz,0,105,shape=shape[1],scale=scale)$value
  sqrt(ea / pi)
  ea/(pi*105^2)


For Model1, the detection probability was 0.64.
For Model2, it was 0.48.

Given that these models have the same detection covariates, why do their detection probabilities differ?

messages.author: 2a3a0c6a456f3043
messages.subject: Re: Detection probability varies between models with the same detection covariates
parts:
Hi Andrew,

I have no experience with distance sampling estimates, but I think the reason is that detection and abundance are estimated simultaneously with a joint likelihood function. Therefore, different covariates in any part of the model can affect the estimates of the other part of the model. Basically, the variation in counts is getting divided up between the two parts of the model (and the error terms) so when the abundance/density covariates are reduced it's possible that some of that uncertainty gets pulled out in detection.

I hope that makes sense and that I'm not too far off the mark. Someone who has more knowledge of the subject can chime in to correct me.
Cheers,
Dan

I think Dan could be correct that the detection and abundance
parameters might be strongly correlated, but your results seem a
little extreme. Do you observe the same thing with other detection

optima. I would suggest trying various starting values.

messages.author: e452970a8244a89b
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Detection probability varies between models with the same detection covariates
parts:
Hi Richard,
  The detection rates still differ for a null and global abundance model when I use fewer detection covariates, but the difference is smaller (e.g., 0.31 versus 0.26 with a single detection covariate).  I reran the original "Model2" with zeros for all starting values and got identical AIC scores and different but nearly identical parameter estimates.  I ran it again with starting values of one and got NANs warnings.  It's not clear to me how to pick "better" starting values or when to trust that the model has converged on a global versus local optima.  

Is it possible that these models are simply a poor fit for the data?  I have been running the chi-square GOF test as shown in the vignette which never suggested any GOF issues (P>0.95):

chisq<-function(fm){
    umf<-getData(fm)
   y<-getY(umf)
   y[y>1]<-1
   sr<-fm@sitesRemoved
   if(length(sr)>0)
      y <- y[-sr,,drop=FALSE]
    fv <- fitted(fm, na.rm=TRUE)
    y[is.na(fv)] <- NA
    sum((y-fv)^2/(fv*(1-fv)), na.rm=TRUE)
  }
(pb <- parboot(Global, statistic=chisq, nsim=100))

However, when I tried the GOF test used in Sillett et al (2012), the models fail (P=0.00):
 freeTuke <- function(fm) {
    observed <- getY(fm@data)
    expected <- fitted(fm)
    sum((sqrt(observed) - sqrt(expected))^2)
  }
GofTest<- parboot(Wind_global, freeTuke, nsim=100, report=1)  

It is not clear to me why two GOF tests suggest such different things, or whether this relates to the extreme differences in detection rates I am observing.

As always, Richard, thanks for your help!

Andrew

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Detection probability varies between models with the same detection covariates
parts:
Hi Andrew,

Since you get the same AIC and estimates, it sounds like you have
found the global optimum. I was wondering if you get similar results
with a different detection function, such as the half-normal. But
after looking at your original code more carefully, I think the
problem has to due with how you are computing detection probability.
When you have covariates on "sigma" (this should actually be called
the scale parameter), then you can't do:

shape<-exp(coef(Model1,type="det"))

Instead, you need to use predict to give you a value of sigma for
specified covariate values. Then you can plug this value of sigma into
the equation for p.

Richard
